source.title: Exactly unsolved problems of interacting 1D fermions

accepted.question_text: In the one-dimensional s-d exchange tunneling model for two metal leads, two effective Dirac-electron species represent the two leads, a chemical-potential bias distinguishes the species, and weak tunneling occurs at a point through an impurity spin with exchange couplings. For this two-channel Kondo-type problem, what are the physical Bethe-ansatz quasiparticle excitations, and what are the bulk and impurity scattering matrices for those excitations?
accepted.context_brief: Bethe-ansatz excitations and scattering in the s-d exchange tunneling model

evidence.quote: In this section we describe two 1D models of electrons tunneling through a point-like defect either by the s-d exchange (Kondo) mechanism, or via the resonanse level (Anderson) mechanism. These models are potential candidates to be solved exactly in the presence of arbitrary external bias by means of the Bethe-ansatz technique.

The same "unfolding" procedure can be applied to the left piece of metal to map the problem eventually to the full axis. We end up with two species of free Dirac electrons on the line, to which we assign the flavor index m = 1, 2.
To summurize, the questions to be answered are: what are the physical excitations in the Bethe ansatz solution of (5)-(7) and their scattering matrices?

accepted.question_text: For the two-channel Kondo model obtained from the one-dimensional s-d exchange tunneling problem, what are the form factors, meaning the matrix elements of fields between Bethe-ansatz excited states, that are needed to evaluate non-equilibrium transport quantities?
accepted.context_brief: form factors for the two-channel Kondo model

evidence.quote: The resulting Hamiltonian is the channel-anisotropic two-channel Kondo model, which was solved by means of Bethe ansatz by N.Andrei and A.Jerez [Phys.Rev.Lett.74 (1995) 4507].
What are the matrix elements of the fields between the excited states (form-factors for the two-channel Kondo model)?

accepted.question_text: For the one-dimensional s-d exchange tunneling Hamiltonian, can the non-equilibrium current be computed by a Boltzmann/rate-equation formula that integrates the difference of the two quasiparticle occupation densities times the squared flavor-changing scattering amplitude, despite the fact that in the original lead basis flavor-changing scattering occurs throughout the bulk and the bias charge is not diagonal on Bethe-ansatz states?
accepted.context_brief: validity of the Boltzmann current formula with non-diagonal bulk flavor scattering

evidence.quote: The non-conservation of flavor is also explicitly present in this term: the in-state |1i ⊗ |1i will be mapped to the supperposition of |1i ⊗|1i and |2i ⊗|2i. So, the scattering of particles of first kind into particles of the second kind occurs not only on the impurity, but also in the bulk.
Then, based on the probabilistic arguments, one employes the Bolzmann rate equation to obtain the current: I ∼ ∫ dǫ[n1(ǫ, µ) − n2(ǫ, µ)]|S12(ǫ)|2.
The flavor z-projection Y0 is not diagonal on the Bethe ansatz states. This leads to some technical difficulties, as well as to the question of the applicability of (42) for such situations.
Can one apply Eq (42) to the model (5)-(7)?

accepted.question_text: For a quantum dot described by a bosonized Hamiltonian consisting of a free boson term, a charging term EC[u(0) - N]^2, and a backscattering term -V cos(2πu(0)), can a form-factor expansion that treats the charging energy EC as a perturbation of the integrable backscattering problem accurately describe the Coulomb-blockade regime where EC is large enough to suppress transport and produce gate-voltage oscillations?
accepted.context_brief: large-charging-energy Coulomb blockade from a form-factor expansion

evidence.quote: Matveev [Phys. Rev. B51 (1995) p.1743] argued that the physics of Coulomb blockade in the quantum dots can be adequately described by the following Hamiltonian, H = H0+HC +H′.
The Coulomb blockade shows up in the oscillations of the ground state energy or the average charge hQi as a function of N, which can be calculated.
The form-factors of sine-Gordon model allow, on the contrary, treat exactly the H′ term, starting from the integrable model H0 + H′ and to perturb it by HC term.

In the first problem it is not clear that the perturbation theory in EC will describe correctly the interesting regime of large EC, although the rapid convergence of the form-factors series leaves us some hope that one is allowed to reach large enough values of EC while the terms of the order of E2C and higher still can be neglected.

accepted.question_text: For a quantum Hall bar interferometer with two constrictions, where the tunneling Hamiltonian contains two cosine terms with amplitudes γ1 and γ2 and the observable is the tunneling current as a function of magnetic flux Φ0 and constriction separation d, how can a form-factor method compute the relevant current-current correlators when the usual odd/even field transformation no longer decouples the fields for two constrictions?
accepted.context_brief: form-factor treatment of a two-constriction quantum Hall interferometer

evidence.quote: Chamon et al [cond-mat/9607195] discussed the device based on the quantum Hall bar with two constrictions which allows observation of interesting interference effects.

The quantity of interest is the tunelling current It(Φ0, d) as a function of flux Φ0 and distance d. For the current It it is sufficient to take its linear response limit, given by Kubo’s formula. The current-current correlators can be obtained using form-factors method and treating one of the cosine terms in (53) as a perturbation of integrable sine-Gordon model.
In the second problem the usual trick of changing the basis of fields to the odd and even fields does not work with two constrictions. The odd and even fields are not decoupled any longer.

accepted.question_text: In a Luttinger liquid with two barriers, after integrating out small island-charge fluctuations in the weak-barrier limit to obtain an effective boundary action with a relevant cos(2√πθ) term of strength aV and an irrelevant cos(4√πθ) term of strength bV^2/(2M), what is the conductance as a function of the effective couplings a and b, and how can the required form factors for the irrelevant perturbation be obtained?
accepted.context_brief: double-barrier Luttinger-liquid conductance from form factors

evidence.quote: In the opposite, weak barrier limit, V ≪ M, following Kane and Fisher one can integrate out small fluctuations of the charge around the value hni and obtain an effective action.
The second cosine term in the last formula is irrelevant for g > 1/4, while the first one is relevant.
It is interesting to find the conductance as a function of a, b by the form-factor method, treating one of the cosine terms in (58) as perturbation.

In the third problem one has to deal with the irrelevant perturbation, for which the form-factors are not quite known. One can in principle overcome this difficulty by an analytic continuation from the space of relevant perturbations.

accepted.question_text: For massless boundary sine-Gordon form-factor expansions perturbed by terms such as cos φ or by the field φ itself, what partial resummation of the most infrared-divergent perturbative terms is needed to make the expansion usable for the quantum-dot, quantum-Hall-interferometer, and double-barrier transport problems?
accepted.context_brief: infrared divergences in massless form-factor perturbation theory

evidence.quote: The basic unperturbed model is the massless sine-Gordon model with the interaction (cosine) term restricted to one point, which is integrable. It is being perturbed by the second interaction term, V (φ), which destroys the integrability.

In all the three problems one has to deal with IR divergences in the form-factor expansion, since the perturbing terms are either cos φ or field φ itself. Such divergences are peculiar for the masssless theories.
The partial resummation of the most divergent terms of the perturbation series is necessary.
